LESSON: CALMING THE STORM

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Miracles of Jesus Christ
Topic 3.2: Calming the Storm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Calming the Storm. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does the miracle of calming the storm relate to challenges facing people today?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the miracle of calming the storm
2. identify the challenges they face in daily life
3. apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CALMING THE STORM
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Calming the Storm helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: CALMING THE STORM
Study Calming the Storm like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the miracle of calming the storm

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the miracle of calming the storm. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the miracle of calming the storm.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Calming the Storm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the miracle of calming the storm. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify the challenges they face in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the challenges they face in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the challenges they face in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Calming the Storm in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the challenges they face in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths

What this means
In this part you learn to apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Calming the Storm is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Calming the Storm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the miracle of calming the storm)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Calming the Storm in your own words. (skill: identify the challenges they face in daily life)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Calming the Storm to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the miracle of calming the storm.
3. Practise this skill: identify the challenges they face in daily life.
4. Practise this skill: apply lessons learnt to overcome the challenges they face as youths.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Calming the Storm from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Calming the Storm: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Calming the Storm?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does the miracle of calming the storm relate to challenges facing people today?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Calming the Storm means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the miracle of calming the storm.
5. Be able to: identify the challenges they face in daily life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
